evals.name: notification-prefs-store
evals.prompt: Add a notification-preferences panel to /dashboard/settings. The preferences (email on/off, push on/off, digest frequency) come from GET /me/preferences for the signed-in user. The panel is made of several client components with instant toggles that share local state through a Zustand store; saving happens with one Save button that persists to PATCH /me/preferences. Tell me where each file goes in this repo and write the code.
expectations: The store is created by a factory function (createStore from zustand/vanilla) that a client provider instantiates once with useState; there is no module-level create() store exported as a hook
The preferences are fetched on the server (a queries.ts/server.ts path that calls verifySession) and passed to the provider as initial-state props; the store itself never calls the backend
Saving is a Server Action in actions.ts with "use server", verifySession, Zod safeParse and updateTag; it is not a store action that calls fetch
The provider is mounted from an app/ page or layout and the page does not await cookies, params or searchParams at its top level (an async child under <Suspense> or equivalent is used)
Consumers read the store with one selector per value or useShallow, never a selector returning a fresh object
The answer deals with client state outliving navigation or sign-out: it resets or re-keys the provider after a successful save, or keys it by user id
No file under features/ imports from app/ or from another feature

evals.name: zustand5-selector-crash
evals.prompt: After upgrading to Zustand 5 this component crashes with 'Maximum update depth exceeded' and 'The result of getServerSnapshot should be cached to avoid an infinite loop'. It was fine on v4: `const { search, setSearch } = useFiltersStore((s) => ({ search: s.search, setSearch: s.setSearch }))`. Why does it happen and what is the right fix in this repo?
expectations: The answer explains that the selector returns a new object on every call, so the default Object.is comparison sees a changed value each time (the cause is the changed reference, not a Zustand bug that needs a downgrade)
The answer offers useShallow (imported from zustand/react/shallow or zustand/shallow) or one selector per value as the fix
The answer does not recommend downgrading Zustand, disabling React Strict Mode or suppressing the error
The answer notes that search filters belong in URL search params rather than a client store in this repository
The answer mentions that createWithEqualityFn / useStoreWithEqualityFn (zustand/traditional) is the other documented option or states that create no longer accepts an equality function in v5

evals.name: persist-hydration-nextjs
evals.prompt: I want to add Zustand persist (localStorage) to a per-feature store in this repo (Next 16.4 with Cache Components, zustand 5). I'm worried about hydration errors. Will I get them, and what should I do? Show the store config.
expectations: The answer gives a safe approach: either explains that reading through useStore hydrates from the initial (server) snapshot so no mismatch occurs and the persisted value appears afterwards, or uses skipHydration: true with persist.rehydrate() in an effect
The answer points out that the persisted value overrides server-provided initial state after hydration (a visible change) or discusses merge precedence
The config includes name, version and partialize, and says the name should include the user id for user-scoped data
The answer recommends validating storage data (for example a Zod-validating PersistStorage) or a migrate function for version changes
The answer states persist is client-only and the server never reads the persisted value

evals.name: blocking-route-build-error
evals.prompt: `next build` fails with a blocking route error on /dashboard/orders. The page does `const { status } = await searchParams` at the top, then renders <OrdersTable> which calls `new Date()` to print 'generated at'. A teammate suggests removing cacheComponents from next.config.ts so the build passes. What do we do instead?
expectations: The answer rejects removing cacheComponents and keeps it enabled
searchParams is no longer awaited at the top level of the page: it is read in a child component wrapped in <Suspense> or passed down as a promise
The answer provides a <Suspense> fallback so the static shell can be prerendered
The new Date() problem is handled explicitly: call await io() (from next/cache) before it so it runs per request, or cache the value, or move it to a client component
The answer explains that uncached or runtime work outside Suspense is what makes the route blocking

evals.name: cache-token-key-review
evals.prompt: Review this code a teammate wrote for the profile card: `async function getProfile(token: string) { "use cache"; return fetchMe(token) }` and they also call `cacheTag(token)` inside it. What's wrong and how should it look?
expectations: The answer flags that cache keys and cacheTag values are stored in plain text, so passing the access token as an argument or tag leaks it
The answer flags the missing cacheLife call
The fix is per-user caching without the token in the key: either "use cache: private" reading the session inside, or a "use cache" function keyed only by a plain userId
The tag is based on a stable id such as the user id (for example profile:<userId>), not the token
The answer says per-user data must not be cached in a shared public cache scope, and mentions that the mutation should call updateTag to expire it

evals.name: redirect-in-try-catch
evals.prompt: This Server Action never redirects after a successful create, it just returns the error state, and the cases list isn't refreshed either: `try { await createCase(session.accessToken, data); redirect("/cases") } catch (e) { return { error: "failed" } }`. Fix it.
expectations: The answer explains that redirect() works by throwing, so the catch block swallows it
The fix moves redirect() outside the try/catch or rethrows non-API errors so the redirect is not caught
The answer calls updateTag (or an equivalent invalidation) for the cases list before the redirect so the list is fresh
Expected API errors are returned as values while unexpected errors are rethrown instead of returning a generic failure for everything
The action calls verifySession and validates input with Zod safeParse (shown or listed as required)

evals.name: client-component-server-import
evals.prompt: ESLint reports 'Feature components must not import server-only modules' in features/cases/components/case-list.tsx, which imports getCases from '../queries'. We tried to work around it by calling fetch() in a useEffect inside the component. What's the right fix in this repo?
expectations: The answer rejects the useEffect + fetch workaround and does not add TanStack Query or SWR
The data is read on the server in the page or a Server Component (app/ composes) using queries.ts and handed to the component as props, or as an un-awaited promise read with use()
The answer explains that components/ and feature components must not import server.ts, queries.ts, lib/dal or lib/data, and why (server secrets and client bundles)
The answer keeps queries.ts/server.ts server-side and mentions Suspense for the streamed part

evals.name: admin-only-billing
evals.prompt: Make /dashboard/billing admin-only. Where should the role check go, what happens to non-admins, and would a single check in the dashboard layout be enough? Look at how sessions work in this repo before answering.
expectations: The role check is done in the data path (queries.ts and actions.ts) through the DAL (verifySession from lib/dal), not only in a layout
The answer says a layout check is not enough (layouts do not re-render on sub-navigation and do not protect Server Actions)
The answer states that proxy.ts is only an optimistic check and not the authorization boundary
The answer notes that the current Session type has no role field (userId and accessToken only) and that it must be added and populated from verified claims
Non-admins get redirect, notFound or a forbidden response rather than rendering the data and hiding it client-side

evals.name: intercepting-modal-refresh
evals.prompt: Our case modal works when clicking a row, but on a hard refresh of /cases/123 we get a 404 / broken page in Next 16. Structure: app/(dashboard)/cases/layout.tsx renders {children} and {modal}; app/(dashboard)/cases/@modal/(.)[id]/page.tsx; app/(dashboard)/cases/[id]/page.tsx; app/(dashboard)/cases/page.tsx. What's missing?
expectations: The answer identifies the missing default.tsx for the @modal slot (returning null) as the cause of the failure on hard navigation
The answer explains that on a hard load the slot's active state cannot be recovered, so default.tsx provides the fallback
The answer states that the full page at cases/[id]/page.tsx renders on direct visit and refresh while the intercepting route renders only on soft navigation
The answer shows the modal being closed with router.back() or a Link and keeps the modal UI as a client component composed in app/

evals.name: dynamic-ssr-false-server-component
evals.prompt: I wrote `const Chart = dynamic(() => import('./chart'), { ssr: false })` directly in a Server Component page and Next 16 throws an error. How should I lazy-load the heavy chart in this repo?
expectations: The answer explains that ssr: false is not allowed with next/dynamic in a Server Component
The fix wraps the dynamic call in a 'use client' component (a client wrapper) that the Server Component renders
A loading fallback (skeleton) is provided for the lazy chart
The answer keeps the charting library import inside the client-only lazy chunk so it is out of the initial bundle, and passes data to it as props
